title: Billions of ghostly neutrinos pass through your thumbnail every second
body: Fusion in the Sun’s core releases neutrinos, tiny neutral particles that barely interact with anything. At Earth, about 65 billion of them cross every square centimetre, roughly a thumbnail, each second, and they keep coming at night because they fly straight through the planet. Almost all pass through you without a trace. Catching even a few takes huge detectors deep underground, where rare collisions produce faint flashes of light.
